subject: Acme renewal & expansion \u0014 call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>

Subject: Renewals  quick call to review usage and options

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well. Our agreement with Redwood is up for renewal in May and we’ve started an internal review of usage and cost. We’ve seen a 3x increase in token usage over the last quarter due to a new summarization workflow and a batch embedding job.

I’d like to set up a 30-minute call next week to:
- review current usage and cost drivers
- understand dedicated capacity vs hosted pricing for our forecasted volumes
- discuss any migration/contract timeline considerations

Can you do Tuesday or Wednesday morning (PST)? I’ll loop in our procurement/legal contacts after the call.

Thanks,
Daniel
Sr. Product Manager, Search & Summarization
Acme Corp

1) Current usage and cost breakdown (we’ll share a short export)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewals  quick call to review usage and options  call recap

Hi Daniel  great to chat earlier. Quick recap and agreed next steps below. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of discussion
- Participants: Daniel (Acme), Lara (procurement  not on the call), Marissa, Ben (SE)
- Current state: Acme is 3x quarter-over-quarter growth in token consumption driven by: recap/summarization feature in product and a nightly batch embedding job for recommendations. Current hosted spend: ~$75k/month.
- Primary pain points:
  * Cost unpredictability during spikes (batch embedding runs)
  * Latency variability impacting end-user summary response times (~300360ms target, currently 400390ms p95 on peak)
  * Need for data isolation and audit logs for regulated search indexes
- Goals:
  * Predictable unit economics at scale (forecast for 34x next 12 months)
  * Consistent sub-500ms p95 latency for summaries in production
  * Ability to run nightly embedding jobs without cost/regression surprises

Proposed expansion path (what we recommended)
1) Move summarization and user-facing generation onto a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) sized for ~3x current throughput to meet latency SLOs and provide cost predictability.
2) Keep batch embedding job on Hosted for now but enable prefix/KV caching and batching improvements; evaluate migrating embeddings to Dedicated if monthly embed spend continues to grow beyond projections.
3) Add Audit & Logging add-on for compliance (required by your security team).

Estimated impact
- Cost: Ben attached a top-line estimate  Dedicated reserved capacity + audit add-on would be ~2025% lower per-token cost at expected volumes vs hosted amortized spend (see attached proposed_dedicated_plan_ACME_v2.pdf).
- Latency: predicted p95 improvement to ~350450ms with Dedicated plus model pinning and optimized kernel profiles.

Agreed next steps (owners & timeline)
- Ben: Share 90-day usage export and the draft cost model (attached). Due: Wed 2026-03-03 EOD.
- Marissa: Prepare a one-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones (Proof-of-concept if needed, procurement, legal review, deployment). Due: Thu 2026-03-04.
- Daniel: Share procurement/legal contacts to start contract review and confirm internal timeline for a decision (target: finalize by end of April).

Attachments included:
- Acme_Q1-usage.pdf (Ben’s export of usage patterns)
- proposed_dedicated_plan_ACME_v2.pdf (cost and configuration recommendation)

Notes / risks
- If embedding spend continues to spike unpredictably, we may need to accelerate migration of batch embeddings to Dedicated or add dynamic burst capacity.
- Legal will need the Audit & Logging spec  Marissa will attach compliance docs when you share your procurement contact.

Next meeting
- Quick sync in two weeks to review MAP and legal feedback. I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 2026-03-16 10:00 AM PST.

Thanks again  feel free to reply here with any clarifying questions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_dedicated_plan_ACME_v2.pdf
Attachment: Acme_Q1-usage.pdf
